summary_en: May-Jul 2026. CX qualitative analysis of power-tools call-center transcripts via Grounded Theory, Python, AI-assisted coding, and Power BI.
summary_detail_en: Timeline: May 2026 - July 2026. Domain: Customer Experience (CX), Qualitative Data Science, AI-Assisted UX Research. Core objective: transform unstructured call center transcriptions into structured dimensions and high-impact operational insights for the power tools segment. Context: customer support interactions contain dense qualitative signals on product defects, usability roadblocks, and user sentiment. Methodology (Grounded Theory, Strauss & Corbin, 1990): (1) Open coding - break raw transcript text into discrete segments with descriptive codes; (2) Axial coding - cluster open codes into thematic dimensions linking conditions, actions, and consequences; (3) Selective coding - unify dimensions into core insight categories for systemic friction and product usage. Technical workflow: Python scripts to clean/parse/structure CSV call logs; AI models orchestrated via Python for inductive coding at scale; synthesis hierarchy Raw Quote -> Initial Code -> Thematic Dimension -> Core Insight; interactive Power BI dashboards for code distributions, thematic density, and dimension cross-tabs. Stack: Python (Pandas, CSV), LLMs for prompt-driven qualitative coding, Microsoft Power BI, Grounded Theory.
